title: Supracondylar fracture
stem: Paediatric area. Ming, 7, fell from the monkey bars onto an outstretched left hand. His elbow is swollen and he won't move it. Interpret the X-ray, assess neurovascular status, and discuss management.

phases.title: Plan
phases.goal: Analgesia, splint, orthopaedics, and warning signs.

review.text: Compartment syndrome threshold. Your notes use an absolute compartment pressure of 25 mmHg. The usual threshold is the delta pressure: diastolic pressure minus compartment pressure under 30 mmHg. The clinical signs (pain out of proportion, pain on passive finger extension) come first.

notes:
Checked against BOAST 'Supracondylar fractures of the humerus in children' (2020) and the Gartland classification.

X-ray: lateral view — posterior fat pad (always abnormal), elevated anterior fat pad ('sail'), anterior humeral line should pass through the middle third of the capitellum (passes anterior to it in an extension-type fracture), radiocapitellar line intact. Ossification centres CRITOE (capitellum ~1, radial head ~3, internal/medial epicondyle ~5, trochlea ~7, olecranon ~9, external/lateral epicondyle ~11 years). Gartland I undisplaced (above-elbow backslab at 90° or less, collar and cuff); II angulated with an intact posterior cortex; III completely displaced — closed reduction and K-wiring (BOAST: within 12–24 h, urgent if neurovascular compromise).

Neurovascular examination and documentation of radial, median (and anterior interosseous — 'OK' sign, FPL and FDP index), and ulnar nerves, and radial pulse and perfusion. The pink pulseless hand needs urgent orthopaedic/vascular input; the white pulseless hand is an emergency (reduce and explore). Compartment syndrome: pain out of proportion, pain on passive finger extension — early; avoid tight flexion and circumferential casts.

Your notes match this (they use a 25 mmHg compartment pressure question; the delta pressure — diastolic minus compartment under 30 mmHg — is the usual threshold).

steps.label: X-ray
steps.hint: Fat pads, anterior humeral line, radiocapitellar line, fracture.

X-ray.r: Posterior fat pad and raised anterior 'sail'. Supracondylar fracture; the anterior humeral line passes in front of the capitellum; posterior cortex intact but the distal fragment is angulated back (Gartland II).
X-ray.mark: Identifies fat pads, anterior humeral line and grades the fracture

steps.label: Neurovascular examination
steps.hint: Pulse, perfusion, radial, median, AIN, ulnar; compartment signs.

Vascular.r: Radial pulse present; hand pink, CRT under 2 s.

Nerves.t: Radial: thumbs up / wrist extension; sensation dorsal first web space
Nerves.do: say thumbs-up & cotton web-L | say thumbs-up & pin web-L

Nerves.t: Median: thumb opposition, sensation index pulp
Nerves.do: say opposition & cotton pulp-L | say opposition & pin pulp-L

Nerves.r: Makes a flat pinch instead of a circle — weak FPL and FDP index.
Nerves.mark: Tests the AIN and finds a palsy

Nerves.t: Ulnar: finger abduction ('crossed fingers'), little finger sensation

Compartment.r: No pain on passive stretch; forearm soft.

steps.label: Plan
steps.hint: Analgesia, backslab not tight, elevate, orthopaedics for reduction and wiring, AIN palsy usually recovers.

opts.t: Pain relief (intranasal fentanyl), a backslab with the elbow not over-flexed, elevation
opts.tz: 我哋會用鼻噴止痛藥俾佢止痛，再用石膏托固定，手踭唔會屈得太盡，同埋舉高隻手。

opts.t: Orthopaedics for reduction and wiring; the nerve weakness usually recovers over weeks to months
opts.tz: 骨科醫生會幫佢將骨駁返正，再用鋼針固定；佢手指嗰啲神經冇力，通常幾個禮拜至幾個月會好返。
opts.mark: Refers for reduction; explains AIN palsy prognosis

opts.t: Watch for severe pain, numbness, pale or cold fingers — tell the nurse at once
opts.tz: 如果佢好痛、手指麻痺、變白或者凍冰冰，要即刻話俾護士知。

opts.t: A tight full cast with the elbow fully bent
opts.tz: 打一個緊啲嘅全手石膏，手踭屈到盡。
opts.r: Hyperflexion and tight casts risk compartment syndrome and vascular compromise.

qs.q: Normal anterior humeral line passes through…
qs.a: The middle third of the capitellum
wrong: In front of the whole capitellum
Through the tip of the olecranon
Through the centre of the radial head

qs.q: Nerve most often injured in extension-type supracondylar fractures?
wrong: Axillary nerve at the surgical neck

qs.a: Capitellum, Radial head, Internal epicondyle, Trochlea, Olecranon, External epicondyle
wrong: Coronoid, Radial head, Internal, Trochlea, Olecranon, External
Trochlea first, then capitellum, then radial head
Flexion type with an intact cortex
An absent radial pulse at the wrist, early on
Pallor and coldness of the whole hand

badge.name: Fat Pad
badge.flavor: Posterior fat pad, check AIN with an 'OK', don't cast it tight.

cards.q: A visible posterior fat pad on a lateral elbow film means…
Pink pulseless hand after supracondylar fracture needs…
options: Discharge with a collar and cuff and fracture clinic review

options: Backslab at ≤90° and collar and cuff
